title: Evening
label: ch:ta-evening
canDo: I can say மாலை for evening and keep it apart from the identically spelled garland word, which is a separate etymology rather than a second sense.

payoff.summary: Complete TA-C27-checkpoint, the chapter's closing checkpoint: say mālai for evening, keep the garland mālai apart as a separate etymology and mark the darkness link as unproven, read நீங்கள் from its pieces, then write நீ, நீங்கள் and மாலை from sound.
payoff.note: TA-C27-checkpoint (sequence 817, TA-PATH-027 order 8, after TA-W11-read-niingal and before chapter 28's first lesson) assesses all five atoms the chapter introduces (5/5). It is the payoff because three of them, ங and ள, the ◌ீ sign and reading நீங்கள் (TA-W11-read-niingal, 815), are taught after the spoken lesson TA-C27-maalai (810), which could honestly assess only its own two atoms (2/5); that lesson stays as the chapter's spoken lesson. TA-W11-read-niingal sits on the earlier TA-PATH-003 segment, so the checkpoint comes after both lessons on the sequence and on the path.
